data.title: Kuwait offers more December naphtha on FOB basis, document shows
data.description:
By Mohi Narayan

Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) has offered 50,000 metric tons of full-range naphtha via a tender on a free-on-board (FOB) basis from its ports, a document reviewed by Reuters showed on Monday.

The cargo is set to load between December 7 and 8 from Kuwaiti ports, the tender - which closes on November 24 - showed.

The state-owned refiner last sold 50,000 tons of full-range naphtha for loading between December 3 and 4 on an FOB basis at a low-double-digit discount to Middle East quotes.

KPC has sold several cargoes on an FOB basis this month mostly at discounts, after previously selling naphtha on a delivered ex-ship (DES) basis at premiums amid disruptions to trade flows through the Strait of Hormuz, market participants said.

Oil companies typically do not comment on tenders.

data.title: Kogan.com Lifts Early-Year Earnings as Mighty Ape Turns Positive
data.description:
Kogan.com Limited has lifted group adjusted earnings by almost 50% in the first four months of its new financial year, as its Australian retail business grew and Mighty Ape returned to positive operating earnings.

Adjusted EBITDA rose 49.4% to $15.2 million between July and October 2026, against group revenue growth of just 3.5% to $161.5m.

For the four-month period, the Australian business produced gross profit of $65.3m, an 18.1% increase that outstripped its revenue growth as its gross margin improved to 46.4%.

The group’s adjusted EBITDA margin reached 9.4%, up from 6.5% a year earlier, reflecting improved gross margins and a smaller cost base at its New Zealand operation.

Kogan.com is meanwhile stepping up marketing for its Kogan FIRST membership program ahead of peak trading, accepting a near-term constraint on margins to build recurring revenue.

Growth Beneath the Headline

While Kogan.com’s Australian business increased revenue 12.2% to $140.6m, its adjusted EBITDA rose 13% to $15m, with its margin holding at 10.7% despite heavier marketing spending.

That spending is directed towards Kogan FIRST and the holiday trading period, with gross sales growth accelerating during the first 20 days of November compared with the July-to-October pace.

“Our marketing investment impacts profitability in the short term, but builds a larger Kogan FIRST membership base, supporting recurring revenues and future earnings growth,” founder and chief executive officer Ruslan Kogan said.

“This is a deliberate investment in our long-term growth.”

Mighty Ape Finds Firmer Ground

At Mighty Ape, the shift away from unprofitable product categories continued to weigh on sales, which fell 31.7% to $20.9m in the July-to-October period.

Yet the New Zealand retailer achieved positive adjusted EBITDA of $0.1m, compared with a loss in the previous comparable period, while gross margin climbed 8.7 percentage points to 33.7%.

The recovery followed a difficult 2026 financial year in which Mighty Ape’s revenue declined 30% to $85.6m and its full-year adjusted EBITDA deteriorated to a $3.3m loss.

By the final quarter of that year it had returned to positive quarterly adjusted EBITDA of $0.4m after reducing inventory from about $21m to $10m and cutting quarterly fixed costs by 30.8%.

Longer-Term Strategy

The change in mix is central to Kogan’s longer-term strategy, which favours membership income, marketplace fees, service commissions, and advertising over inventory-heavy product sales.

Across the 2026 financial year, group gross sales surpassed $1 billion and adjusted EBITDA increased 13.8% to $41.8m, supported by stronger trading and profitability at Kogan.com.

Free cash flow rose 18.2% to $38.3m, leaving $36.4m of cash and no debt after the group returned $34.9m to shareholders through dividends and share buy-backs.

For the medium term, management continues to target a group adjusted EBITDA margin of 8% to 12%, with the latest 9.4% reading placing it within that range while investment in Kogan FIRST continues.

data.title: Mike McGlone Says Crypto Crash Is A Preview Of The 'Everything Bubble' Bursting, Sees Bitcoin At $10,000 Again
data.description:
Key points:
  • Bloomberg's McGlone said most tokens like Dogecoin will probably drop to roughly zero.
  • He said that Bitcoin's summer rally gave fake hope that kept the bear market going.
  • He also sees crude oil falling back toward $40 and copper dropping below $5.

Crypto's slump is just the first sign of a much bigger market bust, says Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone.

In a post on X on Sunday, McGlone said the Bitcoin and crypto bear market that started in October 2025 could show what is coming for most other assets. He named U.S. stocks, gold, metals, commodities, and Treasury yields. "Bear markets can take money from everyone," he wrote. "It's simply overdue reversion."

Why BTC Can Fall To $10,000

McGlone stuck to his long-held belief that Bitcoin will fall to $10,000. He called that level a "good gravity-pull pivot." He said an asset with unlimited supply shouldn't be expected to outperform other assets. This isn't a new call. McGlone has said Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 since at least April 2025.

Bitcoin's price rose more than 1% over the past 24 hours, trading at $60,765 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the 'bullish' zone, while chatter around it stayed at 'high' levels over the past day.

Warns Dogecoin Could Go To Zero

His prediction was harsher for the rest of the market. Most tokens that are tracking nothing, like Dogecoin (DOGE), will probably drop to about zero, McGlone said. He compared crypto to non-fungible tokens (NFTs) and the Dutch tulip mania. From 1634 to 1637, prices of rare tulip bulbs soared and then collapsed from extreme highs.

He also mentioned Strategy (MSTR), the biggest corporate Bitcoin holder. "MSTR is likely to get stopped out," he wrote.

Bitcoin's summer rally is a trap, McGlone said. The coin rose from around $58,000 in June to nearly $86,000 in September. More sharp short-covering rallies like that are likely across markets, he said. He calls them "false hope" that extends the bear market.

Pain Beyond Crypto: Stocks And Commodities Are Next

The pain will extend far beyond crypto, McGlone said. He's looking for a 50% drawdown that likely started at the Oct. 6 high. Now, he expects the S&P 500 Total Return index to end 2026 lower for only the third time since 2009. He said that gold, silver, copper, natural gas and the Nasdaq have made big gains this year and could now unwind.

Other calls he makes include crude oil falling back to $40 and copper dropping below $5. "US housing has peaked along with inflation," he said, adding that "this is a normal cycle of post-inflation deflation."

When Feds Will Step In

McGlone also sees the Fed starting to ease. That puts him at odds with recent market action. According to CME Watchtool data, 93.5% of the markets expect a rate hike in the upcoming December policy meeting.

"The gift of 2026 for investors" is Treasury yields at near three-decade highs, he said.

McGlone cited one thing that would disprove him. U.S. stocks would need to stay near their highest levels relative to GDP in a century or so. "The trading year of a lifetime is more likely to end like a lion than a lamb," he wrote.

McGlone’s call comes at a time when along with Bitcoin, gold and silver has also been under pressure, with Goldman Sachs seeing the possibility of $80.6 billion sell-off in stocks this week.

data.title: Tata Power targets 6.8-GW pumped hydro storage pipeline in India
data.description:
Tata Power plans to grow its pumped hydro storage portfolio to 6.8 gigawatts (GW) through two new projects, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director Praveer Sinha told Moneycontrol in an interview.

The utility is pushing deeper into energy storage while also widening its presence in renewable power and transmission. India is heading into another year of strong growth in electricity consumption and new generating capacity, and storage allows power from intermittent sources such as solar and wind to be held back for use when demand peaks.

The company already has two pumped hydro schemes in development, at Bhivpuri and Shirwata. The two further projects would take the pipeline to 6.8 GW.

Sinha said Tata Power also sees business opportunities in battery storage for homes.

The company intends to keep capital expenditure at INR250bn ($2.7bn) in FY28, the financial year ending in March 2028, according to Sinha.

He added that curtailment of renewable energy, when available green power cannot be fed into the grid, could ease considerably from the July to September quarter of FY28. New transmission lines are expected to start operating by then.

data.title: South Korea's finance minister sees solid growth next year, flags chip volatility risks
data.description:
By Yena Park and Cynthia Kim

South Korea's economy is expected to sustain a solid growth trajectory next year as robust exports and investment gradually spill over into domestic demand, Finance Minister Lee Hyoung-il said on Monday.

Speaking ahead of a news conference in Sejong, Lee said Asia's fourth-largest economy is currently maintaining strong momentum and could achieve growth in the upper-3% range if present trends continue.

He added that consumer inflation is projected to ease next year compared with this year, supported by stabilizing global oil prices, though both upside and downside risks remain.

Despite the upbeat baseline outlook, Lee warned that external risks remain severe, citing regulatory uncertainty surrounding the artificial intelligence industry, geopolitical instability and rising global interest rates. He cautioned that volatility in the semiconductor sector could spill over and amplify broader macroeconomic swings.

data.title: DBS Raises Over $155 Million By Opening Wealth Strategy to Retail Investors
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

DBS has raised more than US$155 million from retail investors through a fund based on a strategy previously available only to its wealth clients.

The multiasset DBS Chief Investment Office Barbell Strategy Fund, which raised 200 million Singapore dollars from the new group of investors, is actively managed through market cycles. The strategy it follows has delivered an annualized net return of 7.9% since its inception in 2019, DBS said Monday.

"With this fund, we are extending a flagship strategy previously available only to our wealth clients to a wider group of investors. As market volatility becomes the new norm, we hope to enable our customers to invest consistently with greater confidence as they grow their wealth," DBS Head of Investment Products (Consumer Banking Group) Chua Yi Wen said.

The DBS CIO Barbell Strategy Fund invests in fast-growing stocks in areas such as artificial intelligence, semiconductors and cloud computing, alongside global bonds and alternatives such as gold and hedge funds.

Write to P.R. Venkat at venkat.pr@wsj.com

data.title: Tata Steel to acquire majority control of APL Apollo Tubes in mega ₹32,266 crore deal
data.description:
Tata Steel Ltd. announced on Monday, November 23, that its Board of Directors has approved the acquisition of a controlling stake in structural steel tube maker APL Apollo Tubes Ltd.

Under a Share Purchase Agreement (SPA) executed with promoter group entity S Gupta Holding Pvt. Ltd., Tata Steel will buy up to 7.38 crore equity shares, representing 26.38% of APL Apollo’s expanded voting share capital, at ₹2,100 per share for a total cash consideration of approximately ₹15,510.61 crore.

The promoter stake purchase will be completed in three distinct tranches. In the first tranche today, Tata Steel is acquiring 2.77 crore shares (9.91% stake) via an on-market morning block deal. The remaining two tranches, one worth 11.9% (3.33 crore shares) and 4.57% (1.28 crore shares), will be completed through off-market transfers on or before March 31, 2028, subject to regulatory approvals and closing conditions.

Triggering mandatory takeover regulations, Tata Steel has simultaneously launched an open offer to acquire up to 7.28 crore equity shares, or an additional 26% stake, from APL Apollo’s public shareholders.

Priced at ₹2,301.40 per share, the open offer could cost Tata Steel up to ₹16,755.66 crore assuming full acceptance. Combined with the promoter stake purchase, Tata Steel’s total shareholding could reach 52.38%, making it the new promoter of APL Apollo Tubes while existing promoters seek reclassification to the public category.

This is breaking news and will be updated with more details.

data.title: Hua Medicine Announces Positive Topline Results from U.S. Phase 1b Multiple Ascending Dose Trial of Once-Daily HMS1005
data.description:
SHANGHAI, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hua Medicine (HKEX stock code: 2552) today announced positive topline results from its U.S. Phase 1b multiple ascending dose (MAD) trial of HMS1005, a second-generation glucokinase activator (GKA). The trial enrolled a heterogeneous population of adults (83% White) with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) in the United States. HMS1005 was generally well tolerated across multiple once-daily dose levels. Serum glucose measurements and continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) showed improvements in glucose control over the 14-day treatment period.

Dorzagliatin, the world's first GKA, launched in 2022. More than 10 million packs have been used in China to treat T2D patients. Dorzagliatin is designed to restore glucose homeostasis by improving glucose sensing, pancreatic secretory function, GLP-1 secretion and hepatic glucose metabolism. This mechanism, together with the potential for disease modification and drug-free remission, informed the development of a second-generation, once-daily GKA for diabetes and other conditions associated with impaired glucose homeostasis and bioenergy deficiency.

HMS1005 is a second-generation glucokinase allosteric activator and a prodrug of dorzagliatin (HMS5552). Unlike dorzagliatin, which is taken twice daily, HMS1005 is designed for once-daily dosing. The Phase 1b study builds on Phase 1a pharmacokinetic findings, which showed efficient conversion of HMS1005 to dorzagliatin and prolonged systemic exposure.

The Phase 1b study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of HMS1005 in patients with Type 2 diabetes. The study enrolled 48 patients across six cohorts and evaluated once-daily doses ranging from 123 mg to 492 mg. The safety, tolerability, and HMS5552 exposure findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 as a once-daily oral therapy for Type 2 diabetes and related metabolic diseases worldwide.

Key Results

  • Pharmacokinetics: HMS1005 was efficiently converted to dorzagliatin (HMS5552) across all once-daily dose groups (123 to 492 mg). The once-daily extended-release formulation showed a favorable dose–exposure profile for dorzagliatin based on peak concentration (Cmax) and area under the concentration–time curve (AUC), compared with findings from a prior MAD study of twice-daily dorzagliatin. These findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 in Phase 2 trials.
  • Safety and tolerability: HMS1005 was generally safe and well tolerated at doses up to 492 mg once daily. No serious adverse events or episodes of severe hypoglycemia were reported, and no clinically meaningful hypoglycemia (blood glucose below 54 mg/dL or 3.0 mmol/L) was observed. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) showed no increase in time below range (TBR) at once-daily doses of 123 mg to 369 mg. 369 mg was identified as the maximum tolerated dose.
  • Glycemic control: Continuous glucose monitoring showed improvements in glucose management indicator (GMI, an analogous measurement of blood glucose levels to HbA1c) and time in range (TIR). Across the drug tolerant once-daily dose groups from 123 mg to 369 mg, the TIR increased and GMI decreased with active parent drug HMS5552 exposure. The largest observed reduction in GMI was 1.48% in the cohort with high impaired beta-cell function, consistent with observations from dorzagliatin studies. The highest observed TIR increased from approximately 35% at baseline to more than 80% after treatment.

Advantage for once-daily prodrug PK profiles: The pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic findings support further evaluation of HMS1005 as a once-daily extended-release oral therapy. The prodrug HMS1005 and active parent drug HMS5552 exposure profiles support a waiver of long-term GLP toxicity study in the HMS1005 clinical development. If confirmed by the regulatory agency, once-daily dosing second generation GKA development will be greatly accelerated.

Clinical Experience with Dorzagliatin

HMS1005 builds on Hua Medicine's experience with glucokinase activators. Dorzagliatin, marketed in mainland China as HuaTangNing (华堂宁®), has demonstrated glucose-lowering efficacy and a favorable safety profile in previous clinical studies and post-marketing use. HuaTangNing (华堂宁®) has been prescribed to over 600,000 patients in mainland China.

At the 2026 American Diabetes Association Scientific Sessions, Hua Medicine presented findings on dorzagliatin from HMM0601, a multicenter post-marketing real-world study involving 2,024 patients with Type 2 diabetes across 80 clinical centers. During the 52-week observation period, no drug-related serious adverse events or episodes of severe hypoglycemia were reported, and the incidence of clinically meaningful hypoglycemia was below 1%. Patients also demonstrated improvements in HbA1c and glycemic control.

At the 2026 European Association for the Study of Diabetes Annual Meeting, further findings from HMM0601 showed that efficacy and safety of dorzagliatin in older adults (aged 65 years or older) and patients with reduced renal function were consistent with those observed in the overall study population.

Interim findings from HMM0701, a prospective real-world observational study, suggested that glucokinase activation may improve TIR and glucose homeostasis in patients with longstanding Type 2 diabetes.

A fixed-dose combination of dorzagliatin and metformin met its pivotal bioequivalence endpoints in recent clinical trials in mainland China. Hua Medicine expects to file a new drug application in 2027.

The clinical experience with dorzagliatin informs the development of HMS1005. Larger, longer trials are needed to establish the safety and efficacy of HMS1005 independently.

Next Steps

Hua Medicine plans to combine data from the Phase 1a and Phase 1b studies with existing clinical and nonclinical data for dorzagliatin to inform discussions with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on the HMS1005 development program. Future studies are expected to assess the efficacy and safety of selected once-daily doses over longer treatment periods, including effects on HbA1c and other measures of glycemic control.

Dr. Li Chen, Founder and CEO of Hua Medicine, said, "The Phase 1b results support further development of HMS1005 and build on our experience with glucokinase activators."

"Drawing on our clinical experience with dorzagliatin, we will continue to evaluate whether HMS1005 can improve glucose control with once-daily dosing. We also plan to explore its potential in other indications, including diabetes prevention, prediabetes, and mild cognitive impairment."

Hua Medicine retains all global rights to HMS1005 and plans to engage with potential strategic and financial partners for development outside China.

About Type 2 Diabetes and Glucokinase

According to the International Diabetes Federation (IDF Diabetes Atlas, 11th edition), approximately 589 million adults worldwide are living with diabetes, a number projected to rise to 853 million by 2050. Type 2 diabetes accounts for the vast majority of cases. Despite the range of available therapies, many patients do not reach or maintain their blood glucose targets, as the disease progressively erodes the body's ability to sense and respond to changes in blood glucose.

Glucokinase (GK) serves as the body's glucose sensor. Found in the pancreas, liver and gut, it regulates glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, hepatic glucose uptake and storage, and the release of incretin hormones such as GLP-1. Impaired glucokinase function is a key defect in T2D. Glucokinase activators (GKAs) are designed to restore this sensing function, addressing an underlying cause of the disease rather than only lowering blood glucose. Hua Medicine's dorzagliatin, approved in China in 2022, is the world's first approved GKA.

About HMS1005

HMS1005 is an investigational new molecular entity and a prodrug of dorzagliatin. It has global patent protection extending to at least 2042. Hua Medicine is developing an extended-release formulation for once-daily oral dosing, with the goal of sustaining glucose control and potentially improving treatment adherence.

About Hua Medicine

Hua Medicine (the "Company") develops and commercializes drugs and is based in Shanghai, China, with companies in the United States and Hong Kong. Hua Medicine works with international partners to develop therapies for unmet medical needs, with a focus on diabetes. Hua Medicine's HuaTangNing (华堂宁®, dorzagliatin tablets) targets the glucose sensor glucokinase, restores glucose sensitivity in patients with Type 2 diabetes, and stabilizes imbalances in blood glucose levels in patients. HuaTangNing was approved by the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) of China on September 30, 2022. It can be used alone or in combination with metformin for adult patients with Type 2 diabetes. For patients with chronic kidney disease, no dose adjustment is required. It is an oral glucose-lowering drug that can be used in T2D patients with renal function impairment.

In February 2026, dorzagliatin (trade name: MYHOMSIS®, 華領片®) was approved for marketing by the Pharmaceutical Service of the Department of Health of the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

In June 2026, dorzagliatin (trade name: MYHOMSIS®, 華領片®) was approved for marketing by the Pharmaceutical Administration Bureau of the Macao Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China.

Based on the International Diabetes Federation's 2025 Diabetes Atlas – 11th Edition, there are approximately 148 million diabetic patients in mainland China, 706,000 diabetic patients in Hong Kong SAR, and 52,000 diabetic patients in Macao SAR as of 2024.

data.title: Pure One Adds 24 Zeus Electric Van Orders Across Expanding Dealer Network
data.description:
Pure One Corporation has received 24 further orders for its Zeus electric vans, lifting its Australian order book to 33 vehicles less than three months after the range launched.

The orders come from a mixture of dealers and end customers, with the additional vehicles scheduled for delivery during 2027 rather than immediate handover.

Priced between $70,000 and $100,000 each, the Zeus range is being marketed to commercial operators while attracting interest from businesses seeking vehicles for specialist conversions.

Pure One has added dealers in Victoria and Western Australia alongside the latest orders as it works towards a national distribution network.

Continuing Launch Momentum

The latest orders follow nine initial vehicle orders announced in October, giving Pure One an early indication of demand beyond the range’s September Australian launch.

Although the company has not disclosed the value or model mix of the latest purchases, the published price range provides a guide to the scale of individual vehicle sales.

For now, the order book represents future deliveries, and the next commercial test will be converting those commitments into vehicles supplied to customers during 2027.

Rather than relying solely on direct sales, Pure One is widening the channels through which fleet operators and other buyers can assess and purchase the vans, with the company identifying dealer recruitment as a central part of that rollout and a target of 10 outlets by the middle of next year.

Diversity of Applications

“What is particularly encouraging is the diversity of applications being considered for the Zeus range,” managing director Scott Brown said.

“Alongside traditional cargo and commercial transport, we are receiving interest in mobile food vending and RV conversions.”

“This represents a significant addressable market opportunity for Pure, leveraging the unique specifications of the Zeus range to generate sales through different market segments.”

Car Sales Express in Victoria and Londy, trading as Purely Commercials in Western Australia, are the newest appointments to the distribution network, extending the company’s presence into markets where commercial customers may prefer to buy through established local businesses.

Expanding that network could give Pure One a broader route to fleet buyers without depending entirely on a single sales channel, and the company is continuing to seek further dealer appointments as it aims for its mid-2027 network target.

New Customer Market

Another source of interest has emerged through AdventureEV, which has joined Pure One as a customer intending to use Zeus vans for recreational vehicle and campervan conversions.

The specialist designs and manufactures electric campervan fit-outs, making the Zeus platform a potential base for uses beyond conventional cargo movement and passenger transport.

Pure One is promoting the range’s payload capacity of up to 1,890 kilograms as a feature for conversion businesses requiring flexibility in their vehicle layouts.

The proposed cargo and passenger configurations are expected to become available in early 2027, broadly aligning the product rollout with the scheduled deliveries from the new orders.

“Our focus is now on maintaining this sales momentum, expanding our national distribution network, and progressing vehicle deliveries in 2027,” Mr Brown added.

data.title: Bitcoin spot ETFs bleed $669 million as outflow streak stretches to four days
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted $669 million in net outflows on November 20. Spot Ethereum ETFs lost another $97.4 million the same day.

That marks the fourth straight day of redemptions for the Bitcoin funds.

The $669 million figure sits at the top of the estimates for the session. Tallies of the day's Bitcoin ETF flows range from about $124 million to $669 million, depending on the tracker. Either way, the money went out, not in.

Ethereum funds had a similar day. Estimates for spot Ether ETF outflows on or around November 20 run from roughly $97 million to $131 million.

The selling did not start on Thursday. On November 19, BlackRock's IBIT led the exodus with a record $541 million in outflows.

On November 20, other issuers took their turn. Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC both contributed to the day's redemptions.

Bitcoin's price told the same story. The asset traded below $62,000 during the outflow stretch, with lows reported between $61,273 and $58,915.

The pressure lined up with a less friendly macro backdrop. Rising Treasury yields and shifting expectations for Federal Reserve policy weighed on markets during the period.

There was one notable holdout. Morgan Stanley's MSBT was among the few products reporting inflows during the turbulence.

The monthly picture is where things get more uncomfortable. Net redemptions from Bitcoin ETFs in November reached about $3.5 billion by mid-to-late month.

That puts the month within striking distance of the record. The current monthly high for outflows is $4.51 billion, set in June 2026.

Inflow days have been scarce. Through mid-month, the Bitcoin funds recorded only two days of net inflows in November.

Still, perspective helps. Since the products launched in January 2024, cumulative net inflows remain positive at roughly $52 billion to $53.5 billion. Total assets under management are estimated between $71 billion and $77 billion.

Spot Bitcoin ETFs arrived in the US in January 2024 and pulled in strong inflows from the start. They gave pensions, advisors and brokerage-account investors a way to hold Bitcoin exposure without touching a crypto exchange or a hardware wallet.

Over time, daily ETF flow data has become a widely watched proxy for institutional sentiment.

The IBIT record is the detail worth sitting with. BlackRock's fund has been the category's flagship, and a record outflow day there suggests the selling is not confined to smaller or pricier products.

Grayscale's GBTC showing up on the redemption list is less surprising, given its history of steady outflows since converting to an ETF. Fidelity's FBTC joining in is a stronger signal that the selling was broad rather than issuer-specific.

The MSBT inflows offer a small counterpoint. Some investors appear to be choosing their entry points selectively, even as the broader group heads for the exits.

The cumulative numbers argue against panic. With net inflows since launch still in the low-to-mid $50 billion range, November's roughly $3.5 billion in redemptions is meaningful but not existential.

Ethereum's ETFs face a tougher setup. They are smaller than the Bitcoin funds, so outflows near $100 million carry more relative weight.

Three things to watch from here. First, whether November breaks June's $4.51 billion outflow record. Second, whether IBIT stabilizes, since the largest fund often sets the tone for the rest. Third, the path of Treasury yields and Fed expectations, which appear to be steering crypto flows more than anything happening on-chain.

data.title: Elon Musk Says 2027 AI Cash Crunch Will Be ‘Nuts’ — Analysts Still See SpaceX Emerging As The Biggest AI Hyperscaler
data.description:
Key points:
  • Musk warned that AI data center delays could create a 2027 cash gap of hundreds of billions of dollars.
  • Dan Ives sees SpaceX becoming the biggest AI hyperscaler as demand outpaces planned capacity.
  • Tesla cut AI4.5 memory by 25% and Musk said AI5 will go to Optimus.

A day after investors lined up to finance $44 billion of AI equipment for SpaceX (SPCX), CEO Elon Musk warned that even a few months of data center delays could leave the industry needing hundreds of billions more.

SPCX shares fell 8% to $127.79 on Friday, bringing their weekly decline to 8%, the steepest this month.

Musk Sees 2027 Funding Gap For AI Companies

Musk warned on Saturday that AI companies could face a cash crunch in 2027 as they wait for costly chips to start earning revenue. He was responding to AI researcher Francois Chollet, who said graphics processors were scarce and getting more expensive to rent. Even after the chips arrive, Musk said, operators still have to power and cool them and get them running reliably enough to bill customers.

“The cash shortage is also going to be nuts next year,” Musk said. “Even cumulative industry delays of a few months between paying for compute and getting it reliable enough to generate revenue will mean hundreds of billions of incremental dollars just for working capital. Where will that come from?”

How Funding Pressure Gives SpaceX More Pricing Power

“I own $SPCX and believe it may be the largest AI hyperscaler in the not too distant future,” Futurum CEO Daniel Newman said. He also owns specialist cloud providers Iren (IREN) and CoreWeave (CRWV). If smaller providers struggle to finance their next data center, he said, SpaceX faces fewer rivals bidding for customers and gains more room to set prices.

“The conditions Elon speaks to are real, but creating a massive spiral for smaller AI clouds is definitely in his best interest. It’s good use of the platform and a good chess move. But it isn’t just some altruistic advice for investors,” Newman said.

Iren had the funding in place and the timing still slipped. Its first Horizon data center went live for Microsoft, and quarterly AI cloud revenue nearly tripled to $200 million. But a customer’s design change and suppliers’ schedules pushed back Iren’s target for bringing more than $4 billion in annualized contracted revenue online. The company now expects to reach that level in January, possibly as late as the end of February, after initially targeting year-end.

CoreWeave, meanwhile, expects customers to help cover the wait between buying chips and earning revenue from them. Earlier this month, it said it expected about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months.

SpaceX Has Financing And A Buyer Waiting

On Friday, Apollo and Goldman Sachs increased a debt offering to about $44 billion after investor orders exceeded the amount available. The financing will pay for Nvidia’s Vera Rubin chips and related equipment, which SpaceX expects to start leasing in the first half of 2027.

SpaceX ended September with 1.7 gigawatts of rated computing capacity, and Musk said he would be surprised to finish 2027 below 13 GW. The company plans to invest more than $74 billion in computing campuses in Texas and Arizona.

For one customer, full delivery triggers a $3.1 billion monthly bill. Anthropic (ANT), the Claude developer that closed its IPO at $83 a share on Friday, expects to receive all the capacity it ordered from SpaceX’s AI unit in December. Spending could hit $120.5 billion through 2029, but either side can cancel with 90 days’ notice after the initial contract periods end in early 2027.

SpaceX Could Become The Biggest AI Hyperscaler: Dan Ives 

SpaceX (SPCX) could become the next biggest hyperscaler, according to Dan Ives, a partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives. He named Musk’s company among the potential winners in the tech sell-off, pointing to demand for AI computing power that he expects will outstrip planned capacity.

Ives put AI-related power demand and backlog at 160 gigawatts through 2029, compared with 80 to 100 gigawatts of capacity the industry plans to build over the next few years. “This technology wave will continue at high speed and the Blue Wave, bears, China hawks are not stopping this 4th Industrial Revolution,” he said.

He expects Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, global market jitters and the prospect of Democrats in Washington taking a tougher line on Big Tech to give skeptics a louder voice. “The bears will feel validated after being doubters of the AI Revolution since early 2023 and will be louder and louder over the coming weeks and months,” he said.

Alongside SpaceX, Ives saw relative safety in established cloud providers Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN) and Alphabet (GOOGL). He also picked Apple (AAPL) and cybersecurity companies CrowdStrike (CRWD), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Zscaler (ZS). In software, he called Palantir (PLTR) and Snowflake (SNOW) leaders.

Tesla Cuts AI4.5 Memory As Costs Rise

Rising memory costs have already changed Tesla’s (TSLA) hardware plans. Musk said on Sunday that Tesla cut the memory in its AI4.5 computer by a quarter. “RAM is super expensive, so we reduced AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB. That will be fine. It’s hard to use 32GB anyway, given memory bandwidth constraints,” he said.

Tesla’s next-generation AI5 chip is headed for its humanoid robot. Asked where the chip would go, Musk said, “It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”

Tesla said that its latest Full Self-Driving software, V15, handles safety-critical situations 25 times better than V14, though drivers still have to supervise it. Musk underscored the size of the claimed improvement, saying, “Some people thought we meant 25% improvement, no we mean 25 times!”

How Do Retail Traders Feel About TSLA And SPCX?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘neutral’ for TSLA and ‘bearish’ for SPCX, with ‘low’ message volume for both stocks.

One user said, “$NVDA $SPCX One way or another, these two are going to ride together. Owning both for this Bull run.”

View this Stocktwits post

Another user said, “$SPCX nope will not go there ….at this price this is a 2 trillion and trades at 58 times trailing sales,.....”

View this Stocktwits post

So far this year, TSLA shares are down 23%, while SPCX shares are 5% below their June IPO price.

data.title: COP31 failure is both healthy and a sideshow
data.description:
By Antony Currie

Climate summit co-presidents Turkey and Australia’s inability to secure a deal overshadows progress on other goals. But the diplomatic debacle may spur reform of a process held hostage by oil producers. Either way, economic realities now do more to drive the energy transition.

Full view will be published shortly.

Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn.

CONTEXT NEWS

The United Nations COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended on November 22 without agreement on the so-called cover decision that the host country and Australia, acting as President of Negotiations, had pushed for.

The EU, Panama, the Marshall Islands and others refused to endorse a cover decision that failed to mention fossil fuels. Some countries also objected to the inclusion in the draft text of carbon capture and storage as an emissions-reduction solution.

Some progress was made on other key goals at COP31, including as many as 90 countries signing up for the "35 by 35" electrification pledge, and the global platform for methane reduction reaching 47 countries.

data.title: Indian shares set to open higher on foreign inflows as AI selloff persists
data.description:
Indian shares are expected to open higher on Monday, extending a four-week winning streak, as foreign investors continued to buy stocks in Asia's third-largest economy amid easing oil prices and a global selloff in AI-linked stocks.

GIFT Nifty futures (GIFc1) were at 25,912 points, as of 7:58 a.m. IST, indicating a positive start for the benchmark Nifty 50 index , which closed at 25,800.6 on Friday.

Foreign investors net bought Indian shares worth 103.08 billion rupees ($1.11 billion) on Friday, as per provisional data. They have invested a record $13 billion so far in November, reducing year-to-date outflows to $18.4 billion.

MSCI's broadest index for Asia Pacific stocks outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) was down 1% with South Korean equities trading 3% lower, as investors questioned the massive, largely debt-funded spending on data centres to power AI models.

India's Nifty 50 has surged nearly 12% this month, compared with a 10% decline in MSCI's regional index, as global investors rotated out of AI stocks and returned to Indian equities after two years of selling.

The rally has also been supported by bullish calls from global brokerage firms HSBC and Goldman Sachs, both of which upgraded Indian equities to "outperform" as funds shifted away from global AI stocks.

"Following the sharp, largely uninterrupted rally in recent sessions, the market's ability to withstand deteriorating global risk appetite and defend key support levels will be critical in determining whether the uptrend retains momentum or gives way to profit-booking," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money.

Brent crude futures were down 0.2% at $92.3 per barrel. The contract has fallen 21.6% so far this month on expectations of easing Middle East tensions and a recovery in regional oil supplies.

STOCKS TO WATCH

** Tata Steel to acquire a 26.4% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for a cash consideration of 155.1 billion rupees and launch an open offer to acquire a further 26% holding

** Automaker Maruti Suzuki India raises prices of select models by an average 0.31% from November 22 due to sustained cost pressures

** IndusInd Bank terminates former top boss Sumant Kathpalia's employment with the bank and is seeking to recover pay spanning his entire tenure, following a disciplinary inquiry

($1 = 92.6700 Indian rupees)

data.title: Malaysia's Exports Could Stay Resilient Into 1Q 2027 — Market Talk
data.description: Malaysia's exports could continue to remain resilient in 1Q 2027, supported by sustained AI-driven demand for electrical and electronic products and stronger energy shipments, says CGS International economist Mas Aida Che Mansor in a note. Global semiconductor sales are forecast to grow 29% in 2027. Domestic electrical and electronics capacity utilization of 87.7% also points to continued shipment growth despite rising base effects, she reckons. Petroleum and liquefied natural gas exports should provide additional support, driven by regional demand and resilient manufacturing activity in China and the Asean region. However, a sharper slowdown in the U.S. or China, weaker crude oil prices and rising trade protectionism could weigh on shipments, she adds. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
